items.summary: In a nonprecedential order, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit affirmed summary judgment for prison officials in Jeffrey Leiser's suit under 42 U.S.C. § 1983, which alleged that his disciplinary segregation violated due process under the Fourteenth Amendment. Assuming a liberty interest, the court found that Leiser received adequate notice of the conduct report, that the hearing committee was impartial, and that the denial of video evidence without audio did not violate due process. The court affirmed on grounds not reached by the district court.

items.summary: On October 27, 2026, the Seventh Circuit issued a nonprecedential order affirming the Northern District of Illinois's dismissal with prejudice, as frivolous, of Marquise Peggs-Bey's suit against JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. The suit alleged that Chase wrongly refused a payment on credit card debt tendered on a payment slip marked 'Accepted for Deposit.' The court held that dismissal with prejudice was authorized regardless of fee payment, that the claims resembled sovereign citizen theories, and that Chase was not required to answer while the case was stayed, and it directed Peggs-Bey to show cause within 14 days why he should not be sanctioned and why a related appeal should not be summarily affirmed.

items.summary: The Seventh Circuit affirmed summary judgment for prison officials Sarah Feltes and Jeffrey Freund in Michael Thompson's suit under 42 U.S.C. § 1983 alleging First Amendment retaliation and interference with access to counsel. The court found no evidence that Feltes took an adverse action, noting that the warden had sole authority to approve disbursement requests over $250 and that Feltes stated she forwarded Thompson's requests to the warden. The court also found no evidence of retaliatory motive by Freund, and the access-to-counsel claim failed because the record did not show Feltes was at fault for the delay. The nonprecedential order was decided October 27, 2026.
items.title: Michael Thompson v. Sarah Feltes, et al

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit denied Miguel Saldana-Yadaicela's petition for review of a Board of Immigration Appeals decision denying his application for cancellation of removal. The court found that the BIA erred by not considering hardship to his eldest daughter, who turned 21 while his appeal was pending, but held the error harmless. The court stated that it lacks jurisdiction to review the immigration judge's factual determinations concerning his daughter's disability and the availability of services in Ecuador and the United States.

items.summary: In an opinion by Judge Willett, the Fifth Circuit affirmed the district court's denial of Mark Lawley's motion to dismiss a Fair Labor Standards Act retaliation suit brought against him individually by former Texas A&M academic advisor Eva Stramaski. UNITED STATES COURT OF APPEALS

No. 25-2121

MICHAEL JACKSON, on behalf of himself and all others similarly situated,

Plaintiff - Appellant,

v.

THOMSON REUTERS AMERICA CORPORATION,

Defendant - Appellee.
items.summary: In a published opinion, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit affirmed the Northern District of West Virginia's dismissal of five class actions brought by Michael Jackson against Thomson Reuters America Corp., Whitepages, Inc., Thryv, Inc., PeopleConnect, Inc., and LexisNexis Risk Solutions, Inc. The actions sought to enforce the private-action provision of West Virginia Code § 5A-8-24(e), which bars disclosure of the home addresses and unpublished telephone numbers of covered judicial and law enforcement officials under circumstances where a reasonable person would believe the disclosure could expose another to harassment or risk of harm. The district court had dismissed the actions after holding that the provision was facially unconstitutional under the First and Fourteenth Amendments, and the appellate court affirmed.
items.title: Michael Jackson v. LexisNexis Risk Solutions, Inc.

items.summary: In an unpublished per curiam opinion, the Fourth Circuit affirmed a 152-month prison sentence, followed by three years of supervised release, imposed on Jeff Allen Adkins by the Southern District of West Virginia after he pleaded guilty to one count of possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine and fentanyl. Adkins argued that the district court erred by using statements he made to police officers as relevant conduct to calculate additional drug quantities and increase his offense level. The court affirmed the sentence for the reasons stated by the district court.

items.summary: In this published opinion, the Eleventh Circuit held that it has jurisdiction over the government's appeal of a sentence reduction granted to Abel Rizo under 18 U.S.C. 3582(c)(1)(A)(i). The court held that, under Rutherford v. United States (2026), the 2018 non-retroactive amendment to 18 U.S.C. 924(c) cannot, as a matter of law, constitute an extraordinary and compelling reason for a sentence reduction. The court therefore reversed the district court's order reducing Rizo's consecutive sentence for his second 924(c) conviction from 20 years to 5 years.

items.summary: In this published opinion, the Eleventh Circuit affirmed the denial of the federal habeas corpus petition of Dorian Frank O'Kelley, a Georgia inmate sentenced to death. The court held that the U.S. Constitution did not require the district court to notify O'Kelley of its intent to dismiss six subclaims as insufficiently pleaded under Habeas Rule 2(c), or to give him an opportunity to amend before dismissing them. The opinion also describes the procedural history, including the district court's denial of reconsideration and of leave to amend.

items.summary: In this unpublished per curiam opinion, the Eleventh Circuit affirmed Alonzo Hill's conviction for possession of a firearm as a convicted felon and his 15-year mandatory minimum sentence under the Armed Career Criminal Act. The court held that the change-of-plea colloquy adequately addressed the core requirements of a knowing and voluntary plea, so there was no plain error. Applying plain-error review to the claim under Erlinger v. United States, the court held that Hill had not shown a reasonable probability that a jury would have found his three prior offenses did not occur on different occasions, citing their timing, location, and drug types.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–128: To take certain Federal land in the State of Washington into trust for the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe, and for other purposes. Public Law 128 Public Law 119–128 140 Stat. 1082 2026-10-20 2026-10-20 United States Governmen
items.summary: Public Law 119-128, approved October 20, 2026, takes approximately 1,082.63 acres of federal land in Washington State, shown as "NPS Parcels to be Transferred to Tribe" on a December 2021 Olympic National Park map, into trust for the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe and includes that land in the Lower Elwha Reservation. The Act exempts the land from valuation requirements, directs the Secretary of the Interior to survey its boundaries, and provides that the land is not Indian lands under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act. It also states that nothing in the Act affects rights under the Treaty of Point no Point of January 26, 1855.
items.title: Public Law 119–128: To take certain Federal land in the State of Washington into trust for the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–130: To provide for the conveyance of certain property to the Southcentral Foundation located in Anchorage, Alaska, and for other purposes. Public Law 130 Public Law 119–130 140 Stat. 1089 2026-10-20 2026-10-20 United States
items.summary: Public Law 119-130, approved October 20, 2026, known as the Southcentral Foundation Land Transfer Act of 2025, directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to convey approximately 3.372 acres in Lot 1A, Block 36 East Addition, Anchorage, Alaska, to the Southcentral Foundation by warranty deed within two years of enactment. The conveyance requires no consideration, imposes no obligations or conditions on the Foundation, and creates no reversionary interest for the United States, and it supersedes any prior quitclaim deed for the property. The Act provides that the Foundation is not liable for pre-conveyance environmental contamination on the property and requires the Secretary to comply with CERCLA section 120(h).
items.title: Public Law 119–130: To provide for the conveyance of certain property to the Southcentral Foundation located in Anchorage, Alaska, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–133: To redesignate the Chiricahua National Monument in the State of Arizona as Chiricahua National Park, and for other purposes. Public Law 133 Public Law 119–133 140 Stat. 1095 2026-10-20 2026-10-20 United States Government
items.summary: Public Law 119-133, approved October 20, 2026, known as the Chiricahua National Park Act, redesignates the Chiricahua National Monument in Arizona as Chiricahua National Park, with boundaries unchanged from the monument's boundaries on the date of enactment as shown on a March 2021 map. The Act provides that references in federal law and records to the monument refer to the park and that funds available for the monument are available for the park. The Secretary of the Interior is directed to administer the park under existing presidential proclamations and the laws generally applicable to National Park System units, and to protect traditional cultural and religious sites in consultation with Indian Tribes, including tribal access and temporary closures on request.
items.title: Public Law 119–133: To redesignate the Chiricahua National Monument in the State of Arizona as Chiricahua National Park, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-11818; Project Identifier MCAI-2026-00490-R] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters AGENCY: Federal Aviation Administration
items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2013-01-05, which applies to certain Airbus Helicopters (Eurocopter France) Model AS350B3 and EC130B4 helicopters. AD 2013-01-05 requires revising the Limitations section of the rotorcraft flight manual (RFM) supplement to reduce the starter generator operating current to 180 amperes (amps) and installing a placard in the instrument panel to indicate the revised limitation. Since the FAA issued AD 2013-01-05, the manufacturer determined the applicability needs to be revised to add helicopters equipped with certain part numbered starter generators and to remove helicopters with certain engines installed. This proposed AD would require revising the Limitations section of the RFM supplement of the existing RFM for the helicopter, to reduce the starter generator operating current to 180 amps and installing a placard in the instrument panel indicating the revised limitation. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters

items.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is publishing a final rule to update the incorporation by reference of several voluntary consensus standards in the Agency's formaldehyde standards for composite wood products regulations under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) due to the standards having been updated or superseded by the issuing organizations. These new standards primarily update test methods and product standards concerning composite wood products that use formaldehyde. EPA is also conforming these updated standards in the scope and definitional sections in the final rule and incorporating by reference a new small scale quality control chamber test method, similar to current methods already incorporated by reference. EPA is also removing one standard that was previously incorporated by reference to avoid redundancy, given that another identical, internationally recognized version of the standard is already incorporated by reference in this rule.
items.title: Voluntary Consensus Standards Update; Formaldehyde Emission Standards for Composite Wood Products

items.summary: This document amends the Table of TV Allotments (table) of the Federal Communications Commission's (Commission) rules by substituting VHF channel 10 for UHF channel 20 at Elko, Nevada in response to a petition for rulemaking filed by Reno (KENV-TV) Licensee, Inc. (Licensee), the licensee of full power television station KENV-DT (KENV-DT or Station), Elko, Nevada. The Media Bureau (Bureau) previously granted a petition for rulemaking submitted by the Licensee to substitute UHF channel 20 for VHF channel 10 at Elko in the table, and subsequently granted a construction permit for its new channel. The Licensee states that it was unable to complete construction of the channel 20 facility by the deadline specified in the Station's construction permit. The Licensee filed the instant petition to amend the table to substitute VHF channel 10 for UHF channel 20 and allow KENV-DT to continue to operate on channel 10 at its licensed parameters and provide uninterrupted service to viewers. The staff engineering analysis finds that the proposal is in compliance with the Commission's principal community coverage and technical requirements, including the interference protection requirements. [official summary truncated; see source]
items.title: Television Broadcasting Services Elko, Nevada

items.opening_verbatim: Title 3— The President Proclamation 11074 of October 22, 2026 Adjusting Imports of Wind Turbines and Their Parts and Components Into the United States By the President of the United States of America A Proclamation 1. Within the past 90 day
items.summary: Proclamation 11074 of October 22, 2026, titled 'Adjusting Imports of Wind Turbines and Their Parts and Components Into the United States,' concurs with the Secretary of Commerce's finding under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 that these imports are entering under circumstances that threaten to impair national security. It directs the Secretary of Commerce and the United States Trade Representative to pursue or continue negotiations with foreign trading partners and to report on progress within 180 days, and states that certain wind turbine components made of aluminum, steel, or copper are subject to tariffs under Proclamations 9704, 9705, and 10962. The proclamation cites the Secretary's findings on grid reliability, cybersecurity risks in imported networked inverters, and radar interference.
items.title: Adjusting Imports of Wind Turbines and Their Parts and Components Into the United States

items.opening_verbatim: Proclamation 11075 of October 22, 2026 National Seafood Month, 2026 By the President of the United States of America A Proclamation Across our Nation's harbors and fishing communities, the unrivaled skill and resolve of American fishermen a
items.summary: Proclamation 11075 of October 22, 2026, designates October 2026 as National Seafood Month and calls on Americans to express thanks to those who work in the seafood industry and to hold appropriate events and ceremonies. The proclamation summarizes actions taken by the current Administration on seafood, including an Executive Order on seafood competitiveness, the launch of the Department of Agriculture Office of Seafood, three proclamations restoring commercial fishing access in the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, and $123.6 million in fishery disaster assistance. It states that the U.S. seafood industry harvests about 8.5 billion pounds of seafood annually, supports more than one million jobs, and generates more than $173 billion in commerce.
items.title: National Seafood Month, 2026

items.opening_verbatim: Executive Order 14438 of October 22, 2026 Decreasing Housing Costs for the American People By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered: Section 1 . Purpos
items.summary: Executive Order 14438 of October 22, 2026, titled 'Decreasing Housing Costs for the American People,' directs the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency to establish a pilot program under which Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac proactively cancel mortgage insurance on eligible single-family loans using automated valuation models, and to expand the title acceptance pilot into an ongoing nationwide program for eligible refinances. The order establishes a Task Force on Manufactured Housing Innovation, co-chaired by the Secretaries of Housing and Urban Development and the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, which must submit recommendations within 180 days on factory-built housing. It also directs the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to reduce interest rates on single-family loans made directly by their departments, consistent with applicable law and available appropriations.
items.title: Decreasing Housing Costs for the American People

items.opening_verbatim: Presidential Determination No. 2027-01 of October 22, 2026 Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended, on Domestic Petroleum Production, Refining, and Logistics Capacity Memorandum f
items.summary: Presidential Determination No. 2027-01 of October 22, 2026, addressed to the Secretary of War, determines under section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended, that domestic petroleum production, refining, and logistics capacity are industrial resources, materials, or critical technology items essential to the national defense. The determination states that industry cannot reasonably provide these capabilities in a timely manner without Presidential action, and it waives the requirements of section 303(a)(1) through (a)(6) for the purpose of expanding such capacity. It authorizes and directs the Secretary to implement the determination, including making necessary purchases, commitments, and financial instruments, and supersedes inconsistent prior directives to that extent.
items.title: Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended, on Domestic Petroleum Production, Refining, and Logistics Capacity
